themes.corpus_position: Dyshidrotic eczema is most commonly due to some sort of contact allergy — common contacts like nickel or other metals, fragrance, soaps, chemicals in nails. Water exposure like hand washing, washing the dishes, excessive sweating can also trigger it — and when you can't find a cause, you can always blame stress. Treatment involves cool compresses and identifying your trigger so you can reduce exposure; for severe cases your dermatologist may prescribe topical steroids.

themes.corpus_position: Minoxidil: 10 out of 10. Biotin: zero out of 10 — it doesn't help unless you're biotin deficient and it can mess up how your labs look, especially for thyroid. For the best results in men you want the 5% twice a day; for women once a day for the 5%. Maximum regrowth can occur at 6 to 12 months of use — people apply it for a few weeks, maybe a few months, don't see growth and give up.
